body:
```suggestion
			Comma-separated list of device names that should be excluded from initializing a RenderingDevice. When used in combination with [member rendering/rendering_device/fallback_to_opengl3], the Compatibility renderer will be used instead if the platform supports it. This setting can be used to redirect users with underperforming or broken drivers to the Compatibility renderer.
			[b]Note:[/b] The name must be an exact match of the full GPU model name (case-sensitive). Use [method RenderingDevice.get_device_name] to retrieve the device's name.
```

I think we should check this first in all cases since initializing the device can be really slow on Windows and Android. Further, some of the devices we will add to the exclusion list are devices that crash while initializing, so failing as early as possible will avoid those crashes.

No device is initialized at this point, _initialize_devices() only fills the list with the possible options; probably a misleading function name to be fair. Actual device initialization is only performed when RenderingDevice is created, which hasn't been created yet by the time this is run.
We are still calling a bunch of driver API functions. My concern is that the devices that are going to crash during init are going to crash before we even check the exclusion list.
